name: Republic of Turkiye

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 769,630 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 85,878,556. Everything inside ne:TUR incl. ~3 million Syrian refugees counted by the World Bank; Northern Cyprus excluded.

activePersonnel.note: IISS as quoted: 355,200 active (Gendarmerie and Coast Guard 161,400 paramilitary excluded). High: CIA Factbook 2025 ~495,000 incl. definitions closer to the World Bank 512,000 (2020) figure.

trainedReserves.note: IISS as quoted: 378,700 reserves; low for the share callable with equipment.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 355,200 minus infantry P roles (140,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Turkey 1939-45 (~1.5 million mobilized from ~18 million, ~8%) for a conscript state with universal male service.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry brigades on ACV/M113. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Turkish_Land_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): ACV-15 and M113; Kaplan/Pars arriving.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Conscripts with professional cadre; Syria/Iraq operations.

count.note: Educated guess. Commando brigades, mountain commandos, gendarmerie-style internal security infantry (army only), marines. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Armed_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Modern light kit, domestic small arms.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Commandos combat-experienced against PKK.

count.note: Altay 5 + Leopard 2A4 310 + Leopard 1 171 + M60T 165 + M60A3 650 + M48A5 750 = 2,051; many M48/M60A3 in storage (low).

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): Mostly old M48/M60 and Leopard 1; Altay entering service.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts with professional cadre.

count.note: ACV-15 IFV 645 + ACV APC 1,433 + M113 family 2,813 + Pars 150 + tank destroyer variants ~856 = ~5,900; high adds ~4,260 MRAPs (Kirpi, Cobra, Ejder).

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Combat use in Syria/Iraq.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Short-range ballistic missiles; Tayfun entering service.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: F-16C/D Block 30/40/50 34 + 172 + 29 = 235; F-35 programme cancelled, Eurofighter ordered 2025.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): F-16 Block 50 with ÖZGÜR upgrade.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional, pilot shortage after 2016 purges.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.25 (obsolete, a generation behind) (slightly above): 1970s F-4E.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: T129 58 + AS532 33 + S-70 70 + CH-47F 10 + UH-1 142 + T625 Gokbey 6 plus navy/gendarmerie S-70B/AB-212 = ~360.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): T129 domestic attack helicopter.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly above): Leading MALE drone producer, Akinci and Kizilelma.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly above): Extensive combat use.

count.note: TCG Anadolu LHD 1 + frigates 17 (Gabya/OHP, Barbaros, Yavuz, Istanbul) = 18.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Mostly 1980s-90s frigates, new I-class.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: Ada corvettes 4 + MCM 11 + landing ships 5 + fast attack craft 17 + fast patrol 7 = 44.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: 12-14 Type 209 / Preveze / Gur; Reis (Type 214) class entering service.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Type 209 old; Reis AIP new.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: Atilgan 70 + Zipkin 35 launchers (~6 per battery, ~18) + Hisar-A/O, Siper and S-400 (4 batteries, not operational) + towed Korkut/Oerlikon = ~45 batteries.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Domestic Hisar/Siper arriving under Steel Dome.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

commandQuality.note: Rubric commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders) (slightly below): Experienced staff (Syria, Iraq, Libya operations), but 2016 coup-attempt purges removed many senior officers.

cohesion.note: Rubric cohesion 0.75 (professional with strong unit identity) (slightly below): National conscript army with strong identity; commandos elite.

morale.note: Rubric morale 0.75 (motivated, recent victories) (slightly below): Motivated; recent successful operations, nationalist support.

weapons.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Domestic SOM/Bora/Tayfun, armed drones, MAM-L micro-munitions.

armor.note: Anchor 9: Altay entering service; M60T and Leopard 2A4 upgrades.

ships.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: TCG Anadolu drone carrier, MILGEM corvettes/I-class frigates.

fortification.note: Anchor 9: Steel Dome GBAD under construction.

communications.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Domestic tactical radios (Aselsan), satellites.

isr.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Akinci/Anka persistent ISR, Gokturk satellites.

air.note: Anchor 9: F-16 Block 50, no 5th generation (KAAN in test).

cyber.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: National cyber units.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 2,564,269,207,412 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 85,878,556 = 29,859. Range +/-10%.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 3,203,334,425,249 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 2,564,269,207,412 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 1.91% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 1.84% in 2024, 1.81% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 24.0% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Near self-sufficient; large fruit/vegetable/flour exporter, imports grain.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 42,846,961 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 7.359% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 630,616. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

armor.note: Educated guess. Altay series production (BMC) began slowly with Korean powerpack. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Turkish_Land_Forces)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Otokar/FNSS/BMC/Nurol output incl. exports.

artillery.note: Educated guess. MKE Firtina-II and MLRS.

drones.note: Educated guess. Baykar/TAI MALE drones (Group 2+), large share exported.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Istanbul-class frigates and MILGEM hulls.

roadKm.note: As quoted: 438,633 km of which 344,403 paved (2024).

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 10,546 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 6,842 thousand DWT under the Turkish flag. High is an educated guess for Turkish-owned tonnage under foreign flags.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cross-border operations sustained 30-150 km deep into Syria/Iraq.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. Turkey hosts US B61 bombs at Incirlik (FAS host list), but has no Turkish aircraft certified for them; not counted.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: mountainous Anatolia gives depth, harsh eastern winter, strong population support.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:TUR (Northern Cyprus excluded). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from the Wikipedia Turkish Land Forces equipment list, active Turkish military aircraft list and active navy ship list; drones = Group 2+ only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Region tagged europe for this wave; Turkey bridges Europe and the Middle East.
